title: Northgate Purchases & Returns — Purchase Records and the Membership Presented
content:
**Clause.** A member may hold any number of purchases on any channels of Northgate Purchases & Returns; there is no limit on how many a member holds. Every purchase is its own record with its own lines, and nothing on one purchase — refunds, adjustments, rebates or fees — is ever booked against another.

**Acceptance by membership status.**

1. On a channel that sells only to holders of an active membership, a purchase is accepted only when the membership presented has status active on the order date. The basis is the system record of that membership — its status on the order date, matched by its membership number to the membership on the purchase — not the member's own account of it.
2. On a channel that also sells to non-members, the purchase is accepted whatever the membership status, and the non-member surcharge applies when the membership on the purchase did not have status active on the order date.
3. A channel open only to business-segment memberships accepts only a business-segment membership.

## The clause as a table

| Channel sells only to active memberships | Membership on the purchase active on the order date | Result |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | purchase accepted |
| yes | no | purchase not accepted |
| no | yes | purchase accepted, no non-member surcharge |
| no | no | purchase accepted, non-member surcharge applies |

## Points of judgement

- **One purchase, one ledger.** A member with three open purchases has three separate records; a refund owed on the first is never netted against a fee on the second.
- **The date that counts.** Status is read on the order date of the purchase, not on the day the member calls.
- Hypothetical case: a membership that expired the day before the order date was not active on the order date. On a members-only channel that purchase is not accepted; on the Northgate.com Ship-to-Home Order it is accepted and carries the non-member surcharge.
